words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Pain-free' / 'painless' dentistry (some states prohibit; e.g., Idaho per ADA guide; GOLD-dental-051)
'Specialist' / 'practice limited to' unless the dentist meets the ADA-recognized specialty and state rules (ADA Code 5.H; state laws)
Unsubstantiated superiority ('best dentist in town', '#1') - some states ban superiority claims outright (e.g., Florida per ADA guide)

'Lifetime guarantee' or 'lifetime whitening' without stating whose life and all conditions (16 CFR 239.4; some states prohibit guarantees in dental ads, e.g., Illinois per ADA guide) (GOLD-dental-026/028)
'Your benefits expire December 31' as a universal statement - say 'if your plan resets on a calendar year'
'$0 cleanings' / 'Free with insurance' without saying it depends on the patient's coverage (GOLD-dental-020/065); never waive copays routinely
'$350 value' / '(a value of $X)' unless that is the price actually charged (16 CFR 233) (GOLD-dental-023)
Patient photos, names or before/afters without written HIPAA authorization; composite or stock 'results'
Government/insurer look-alike notices about benefits (39 USC 3001)
compliance_notes: FTC Act s.5 + ADA Code 5.F: no false or misleading claims; health claims need competent and reliable scientific evidence; claims must be substantiated before printing.

Fee ads vary by state (verified via ADA's legal guide; client must confirm current rules): Florida rule 64B5-4.003 requires a 'minimum fee' disclaimer, a stated period (or 90 days) and ADA CDT description/code for advertised fees; Indiana requires the full and discounted price and period; California requires disclosure of everything included and excluded, and for discounts the non-discounted fee, the discount, duration and eligible groups.

Florida s. 456.062 (verified, 2026 statutes): any ad for a free, discounted or reduced-fee service by a dentist (ch. 466) and other listed licensees must print, in capital letters and clearly distinguishable: 'THE PATIENT AND ANY OTHER PERSON RESPONSIBLE FOR PAYMENT HAS A RIGHT TO REFUSE TO PAY, CANCEL PAYMENT, OR BE REIMBURSED FOR PAYMENT FOR ANY OTHER SERVICE, EXAMINATION, OR TREATMENT THAT IS PERFORMED AS A RESULT OF AND WITHIN 72 HOURS OF RESPONDING TO THE ADVERTISEMENT FOR THE FREE, DISCOUNTED FEE, OR REDUCED FEE SERVICE, EXAMINATION, OR TREATMENT.'

Illinois (per ADA guide, 225 ILCS 25/45): a dentist may not charge a new patient for any service provided at the time of an advertised free exam. New Jersey (N.J.A.C. 13:30-6.2): free/discounted services must be offered equally to all eligible patients regardless of third-party coverage.

Medicare/Medicaid patients (OIG, verified): free items/services to beneficiaries must stay within nominal value ($15 per item, $75 per patient per year, no cash equivalents) unless an exception applies; routine copay/deductible waivers and 'no out-of-pocket' ads are suspect (OIG Special Fraud Alert). Applies to 'Accepting Medicaid/Medicare' cards (GOLD-dental-017/064) that also offer freebies.
Social-coupon/referral-fee arrangements may be fee-splitting under state rules and ADA Code 4.E; referral gifts to patients vary by state.

HIPAA (verified): mailing about the practice's own services to its own patients is not 'marketing' needing authorization (unless a third party pays for the communication). Patient photos/testimonials need written authorization. Keep treatment details off the outside of a postcard.

Testimonials and before/afters: 16 CFR 255 (results shown are taken as typical; disclose generally expected results); California BPC 651 requires comparable before/after presentation, the procedures named, and the statement that the same results may not occur for all patients.
Financing ('$0 down braces', '$X/mo'): Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24 trigger terms apply (see roofing.json/hvac.json for the full rule); 'Financing available' is the safe phrase.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer.why: Cost is the top barrier (59%); a clear all-in price removes uncertainty. The most common gold-set offer ($29-$199 exam/X-rays/cleaning).
emotion_by_offer.reinforcing_photo: Real hygienist with a relaxed patient in a bright operatory
emotion_by_offer.what_backfires: Stacking 4+ offers; vague 'specials' with no price; '(a $350 value)' anchors that aren't real prices

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold set is dominated by stacked multi-offer fronts (GOLD-dental-012/031/047/051) and MMR-284 credits a multi-offer card vs roofing round-5 votes for one offer per card
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: No dental votes yet; votes from roofing are cross-vertical and directional. Default to one hero offer with secondary offers on the back, and test. Patrick's dental votes will override once they exist.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: 'Pain-free dentistry' (GOLD-dental-051) and 'lifetime guarantee' (GOLD-dental-026) vs state dental rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: use 'comfort-focused' and spell out any warranty terms; skip guarantees where the state bans them.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: '$0 cleaning' / 'free with insurance' (GOLD-dental-020/065) vs OIG copay-waiver alert and NJ equal-offer rule
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: say 'Most PPO plans cover cleanings at 100%; we'll check yours' only if true, and never waive copays routinely.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Fear angle vs 'stay positive' healthcare conventions
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Emotion-agnostic: the fear data (72.6%) supports naming fear when paired with a real comfort action (EPPM). The client chooses.
